slides.0.title: The Five Key White Grapes
slides.0.subtitle: Level 1 · Portugal's Core White Grape Varieties
slides.0.points.0.text: Portugal's most internationally known white variety, a specialty of the Monção and Melgaço sub-regions of Vinho Verde
slides.0.points.1.text: High acidity and pronounced minerality, found throughout Portugal and suited to ageing
slides.0.points.2.text: The soul of Dão whites, aromatic and complex with outstanding ageing potential
slides.1.title: Portugal's Five Core White Grapes
slides.1.items.0.desc: The same as Spain's Albariño. Its Portuguese home is Monção/Melgaço in Minho. Intensely aromatic with peach and citrus, naturally high acidity, the world's best-known Portuguese white variety
slides.1.items.1.desc: A high-acid variety with outstanding minerality. The main variety of Bucelas DOC and widely used in white blends from Lisboa, Alentejo and Algarve. Gains much complexity with age
slides.1.items.2.desc: Dão's flagship white variety. Intricate aromas and elegant structure; with age it shows cream, nut and mineral complexity, rivalling white Burgundy
slides.1.items.3.desc: Portugal's most widely planted white variety (especially in Tejo and Lisboa). Aromatic and easy-drinking with aniseed and floral notes, suited to young, fresh whites
slides.1.items.4.desc: An important Vinho Verde variety (Lima sub-region). Its name means "laurel"; it has floral, honeyed and citrus character, fresh and pleasant
slides.2.question: Where is Alvarinho (Albariño)'s most important Portuguese region?
slides.2.options.1: The Monção/Melgaço sub-regions of Vinho Verde
slides.2.explanation: Alvarinho is the specialty of the Monção and Melgaço sub-regions of Vinho Verde DOC, where it reaches its highest quality. The same variety is called Albariño in Spain.
slides.3.message: Congratulations on completing Lesson 8! You have mastered Portugal's five core white grapes.
slides.3.keyPoints.0: Alvarinho (= Albariño): the world's best-known Portuguese white variety, a Minho specialty
slides.3.keyPoints.1: Arinto: high acidity and minerality, ages well, found throughout Portugal
slides.3.keyPoints.2: Encruzado: Dão's flagship white, comparable to Burgundy
slides.3.keyPoints.3: Fernão Pires: the most widely planted, aromatic and easy-drinking
slides.3.keyPoints.4: Loureiro: the floral signature of Vinho Verde
